title: Protein synthesis
summary: How does the code in a gene become a protein?
cards.0.h: From gene to protein: the central dogma
cards.0.p: A region of DNA that carries the instructions for making a protein is called a gene. This information is first copied into RNA. This is called transcription. Then it is translated into the language of amino acids. This is called translation.
cards.0.svg#9: exception: retroviruses make DNA from RNA
cards.0.key: This flow of information from DNA to RNA and from RNA to protein is called the central dogma. Some genes code for RNA rather than protein.
cards.1.p: RNA polymerase binds to the promoter region at the start of the gene and opens the DNA. It reads only the template strand and extends the RNA in the 5'→3' direction. A U is placed opposite each A in the template.
cards.1.key: No primer is needed in this process. At the end region, the RNA comes off and the DNA closes again. The mRNA is a copy of the coding strand with U written in place of T.
cards.1.once.soru: If the template DNA strand is 3'-TAC-5', what is the mRNA?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: A pairs with T, U pairs with A and G pairs with C.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: RNA has no T. U pairs with A.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: This is a copy of the template. The mRNA is the complement of the template.
cards.2.p: In eukaryotes, transcription happens in the nucleus. Along the way, introns are cut out, exons are joined and the mRNA moves into the cytoplasm. Prokaryotes have no nucleus. That is why transcription and translation happen at the same time.
cards.2.key: Mature mRNA passes through the nuclear pores. In prokaryotes, ribosomes attach to mRNA that is still being made.
cards.2.once.soru: In a bacterium, can ribosomes start reading an mRNA while it is still being written?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: A bacterium has no nuclear envelope. So writing and reading happen in the same place at the same time.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.yazi: No, it must leave the nucleus
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: Bacteria have ribosomes too, because every cell makes proteins.
cards.3.p: mRNA is read three bases at a time, with no gaps. Each triplet is called a codon, and there are 4³ = 64 codons. The AUG codon starts synthesis and codes for methionine. UAA, UAG and UGA stop synthesis.
cards.3.key: Stop codons do not code for amino acids. The other 61 codons code for the 20 kinds of amino acids.
cards.4.p: More than one codon can code for the same amino acid. That is why the genetic code is redundant. But a codon always stands for just one amino acid. The code is the same in nearly all living things, so it is universal.
cards.4.svg#12: GCU is alanine in bacteria and in humans.
cards.4.svg#13: exception: a few codons differ in mitochondria
cards.4.key: That is why some base changes do not affect the protein. There are a few exceptions, such as mitochondria.
cards.4.once.soru: There are 64 codons, but only 20 amino acids. How is that possible?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.yazi: One amino acid can have several codons
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: For example, 6 different codons code for leucine. This is called a redundant code.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.yazi: Some codons code for two amino acids
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: A codon always stands for just one amino acid. Otherwise the protein would be ambiguous.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.yazi: The extra codons are not used
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: Each of the 61 codons codes for an amino acid, and the remaining 3 are stop codons.
cards.5.p: tRNA carries amino acids to the ribosome. One end of a tRNA holds a specific amino acid, and the other end has a three-base anticodon. The anticodon pairs with the codon on the mRNA.
cards.5.key: The amino acid is attached to the tRNA by a special enzyme, using ATP. There is no tRNA for the stop codons.
cards.5.once.soru: If the codon on the mRNA is AUG, what is the anticodon of the tRNA that pairs with it?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: A pairs with U, U with A and G with C.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: A sequence does not pair with itself. The anticodon must be complementary.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: T is found only in DNA. tRNA has U.
cards.6.p: The ribosome is a structure without a membrane where translation takes place. The small subunit holds the mRNA. In the large subunit, peptide bonds form, and tRNAs sit in the A, P and E sites.
cards.6.svg#8: rRNA + protein, no membrane. Prokaryote 70S, eukaryote 80S
cards.6.key: A ribosome is made of rRNA and protein, and its subunits come together only during synthesis. A prokaryotic ribosome (70S) is smaller than a eukaryotic one (80S).
cards.6.once.soru: If you compare a bacterium with a human cell, which one has ribosomes?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: Ribosomes have no membrane and make proteins in both bacteria and human cells. A bacterial ribosome (70S) is smaller.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: Bacteria make proteins too, and they have ribosomes.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: In a human cell, ribosomes are found both in the cytoplasm and on the rough ER.
cards.7.p: The small subunit finds the AUG codon on the mRNA, and the initiator tRNA carrying methionine pairs with it. Then the large subunit joins. The initiator tRNA sits in the P site, and the A site stays empty.
cards.7.key: The anticodon of the initiator tRNA is UAC. The first methionine may be cut off later in the mature protein.
cards.7.once.soru: Which amino acid does the synthesis of every protein start with?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: The start codon, AUG, codes for methionine.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: The codons for leucine are not start codons.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: The codons for glycine are not start codons.
cards.8.p: A new tRNA arrives at the A site. The chain in the P site is transferred to the amino acid in the A site by a peptide bond. Then the ribosome shifts by one codon, and the empty tRNA leaves from the E site.
cards.8.key: A water molecule is released as each peptide bond forms. The tRNA holding the chain moves to the P site, and the cycle repeats. The ribosome reads the mRNA in the 5'→3' direction.
cards.9.p: When a stop codon reaches the A site, there is no tRNA that pairs with it. Instead, a release factor binds and the chain is released. The subunits separate, and the polypeptide folds into a working protein.
cards.9.key: A stop codon does not code for an amino acid. So no amino acid is added to the chain for it.
cards.9.once.soru: The UAA stop codon has reached the ribosome's A site. What happens now?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: No tRNA comes to a stop codon. A protein factor binds and releases the chain.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.yazi: One more amino acid is added
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: A stop codon does not code for an amino acid.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: The ribosome does not skip the stop codon. Synthesis ends there.
cards.10.p: Many ribosomes can read one mRNA at the same time. This is called a polyribosome. Free ribosomes make the proteins that will stay in the cytoplasm. Ribosomes on the rough ER make the proteins that will be secreted.
cards.10.key: Many copies of the same protein are made from one mRNA in a short time. The ribosome closest to the 3' end carries the longest chain.
cards.10.once.soru: A pancreas cell secretes insulin. On which ribosomes is insulin made?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: Proteins to be secreted are made on rough ER ribosomes and packaged in the Golgi.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: Free ribosomes make the proteins that stay inside the cell.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: mRNA is written in the nucleus. Protein is made on ribosomes.
cards.11.p: The mRNA coding for a polypeptide of n amino acids has n + 1 codons, counting the stop codon. That makes 3(n + 1) nucleotides. The number of peptide bonds in the chain, and of water molecules released, is n − 1.
cards.11.svg#21: coding region only, no introns or end regions
cards.11.key: The gene's double-stranded DNA has at least 6(n + 1) nucleotides. n tRNAs come to the ribosome, because no tRNA comes to the stop codon.
cards.11.etk.soru: Change the number of amino acids in the polypeptide. Only the coding region is counted.
cards.12.p: If a single base in DNA changes, it is a point mutation. In a silent mutation, the amino acid stays the same. In a missense mutation, the amino acid changes. Sickle-cell anemia is an example. In a nonsense mutation, a stop codon forms.
cards.12.svg#27: Sickle-cell anemia: Glu → Val in β-globin
cards.12.key: A nonsense mutation shortens the protein and is often more harmful than a missense mutation.
cards.13.p: If one or two nucleotides are inserted or deleted, the reading frame shifts. Then all the codons after it change, and an early stop codon often appears.
cards.13.svg#19: every codon after the deletion changes
cards.13.svg#20: a 1 or 2 base shift: the frame breaks
cards.13.key: The resulting protein is usually useless. If three nucleotides are inserted or deleted, the reading frame is kept.
cards.14.p:
• Information flows from DNA to mRNA, and from mRNA to protein.
• In eukaryotes introns are removed, and in prokaryotes the two processes happen at the same time.
• 64 codons code for 20 amino acids. AUG starts, and stop codons end.
• n amino acids have n − 1 peptide bonds.
• A mutation can be silent, missense, nonsense or a frameshift.
cards.14.svg#9: n amino acids → n + 1 codons → 3(n + 1) nucleotides
cards.14.etk.soru: Put the steps from gene to protein in a eukaryotic cell in order.
quiz.0.q: A mature mRNA codes for a single-chain polypeptide of 200 amino acids. How many nucleotides are in its coding region, counting the stop codon?
quiz.0.e: 200 amino acids need 200 codons, and with the stop codon there are 201 codons. 201 × 3 = 603 nucleotides.
quiz.1.q: The coding region of an mRNA is 612 nucleotides, counting the stop codon. How many tRNA molecules come to the ribosome while a polypeptide is made from this mRNA?
quiz.1.e: There are 612 / 3 = 204 codons. No tRNA comes to the stop codon, and one tRNA brings each of the 203 amino acids. So 203 tRNAs come.
quiz.2.q: Match each base change with its type of mutation. UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.
quiz.2.e: If the same amino acid comes, the mutation is silent. If a different amino acid comes, it is missense. UGA is a stop codon, so the protein stays short. This is a nonsense mutation. When a nucleotide is deleted, every codon after it changes. This is called a frameshift.
quiz.3.q: The template strand of a gene has the sequence 3'-TAC GGA-5'. Which mRNA sequence is made from this region?
quiz.3.e: The mRNA is complementary to the template strand and runs in the opposite direction. A pairs with T, U with A and C with G. RNA has no T.
quiz.3.y.1: mRNA has uracil in place of thymine. A sequence with T is DNA and cannot be RNA.
quiz.3.y.2: You wrote the same sequence as the template. The mRNA is complementary to the template. A pairs with T, U with A and C with G.
quiz.3.y.3: The bases are right, but the ends are reversed. The mRNA runs opposite to the template, so its 5' end is opposite TAC.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Write mRNA from DNA, read the codons and grow the chain on the ribosome.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Information is first copied from DNA into RNA. This is called transcription. RNA polymerase reads only the template strand and adds complementary RNA nucleotides.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.soru: Which base goes opposite an A in the template strand of the mRNA?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: T is found only in DNA. In RNA, another base takes its place.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: RNA has no thymine. Uracil (U) goes opposite A.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A base does not pair with itself. The partner of A is a pyrimidine.
A:adimlar.1.metin: mRNA is read three bases at a time, and each triplet is called a codon. UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons. Read the codons in order and go on until the stop codon.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: 5 codons gave 4 amino acids: Met, Ala, Trp and Lys. There are 3 peptide bonds between them.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Play the ribosome and watch how the tRNAs pass through the A, P and E sites.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: When the ribosome shifts by one codon, from which site does the empty tRNA that has let go of its chain leave?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The A site is where a newly arriving tRNA enters.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The P site is where the tRNA holding the chain sits. After the shift, the tRNA from A moves there.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The empty tRNA leaves from the E (exit) site.
A:adimlar.3.metin: One codon codes for each amino acid, and there is also a stop codon at the end. Each codon is 3 nucleotides. Change the number of amino acids and make the mRNA's coding region 453 nucleotides.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: 150 amino acids and one stop codon make 151 codons. 3 · 151 = 453 nucleotides. The chain has 150 − 1 = 149 peptide bonds, and one water molecule was released for each bond.
A:adimlar.4.metin: In the β-globin chain of hemoglobin, amino acid 6 is glutamic acid (Glu). Change the middle base of this amino acid's codon and see what happens to the red blood cell.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: The GAG codon became GUG, and valine (Val) took the place of glutamic acid. This single change distorts the shape of hemoglobin, and red blood cells take on a sickle shape. This is called sickle-cell anemia. It is a missense point mutation.
A:adimlar.5.metin: Now change the third base of the same codon: let GAG become GAA.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: Why did this base change not affect the protein?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In sickle cell, the middle base changed and the protein changed. What decides is not the position of the base but the meaning of the new codon.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The genetic code is redundant. More than one codon can code for an amino acid. GAG and GAA both code for Glu, so the protein stays the same. This is called a silent mutation.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.yazi: A codon codes for several amino acids
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: It is the other way around. A codon always stands for one amino acid, but an amino acid can have more than one codon.
A:adimlar.6.metin: What happens if a base is inserted or deleted? Insert a single U into the mRNA before the third codon and watch the reading.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: What happened to the protein when a single base was inserted?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: That happens in a point mutation. Look at the codons after the insertion.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: When you turn on the switch, you can see that the chain gets shorter.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.yazi: The frame shifted and the chain got shorter
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The reading frame shifted by one letter. A UAA stop codon formed after GCU, and the protein stopped at 2 amino acids.
A:kapanis.0: Information flows from DNA to mRNA (transcription), and from mRNA to protein (translation).
A:kapanis.1: The mRNA is the complement of the template strand. A U goes opposite each A in the template.
A:kapanis.2: There are 64 codons. AUG starts synthesis and codes for methionine. UAA, UAG and UGA stop synthesis, and the remaining 61 codons code for 20 amino acids.
A:kapanis.3: A chain of n amino acids needs n + 1 codons and 3(n + 1) mRNA nucleotides. The chain forms n − 1 peptide bonds, and n − 1 water molecules are released.
A:kapanis.4: A mutation can be silent, missense (sickle cell), nonsense or a frameshift.
